**Understanding Your Recent Seizures**

It is completely understandable to feel concerned after experiencing two generalised seizures within the last three months. A generalised seizure involves the entire brain at once, often causing loss of consciousness, stiffening, or jerking movements. While these episodes are frightening, they are a medical condition that specialists can evaluate and manage.

Currently, we do not have specific details about your symptoms during those events or any existing test results. This means we cannot yet determine the exact cause, or etiology, of the seizures. It is important to distinguish between what we know and what we do not. We know you had two events. We do not yet know if they were caused by a structural issue in the brain, a genetic factor, or another trigger. Because we lack specific MRI brain scan reports or EEG (electroencephalogram) results from the time of the events, we cannot rule out underlying causes. These tests are not negative; they are simply not available in our current records. An MRI looks for physical changes in the brain, while an EEG measures electrical activity to see if there is a tendency for seizures.

Your specialist follow-up plan will likely involve gathering these missing pieces of information. The team may request new imaging or repeat an EEG to get a clearer picture. They will also review your full medical history to look for potential triggers. This process is about building a complete understanding so that the right management strategy can be developed.

Regarding safety, you should take practical precautions while the cause is being investigated. Avoid swimming alone, climbing heights, or operating heavy machinery. It is crucial to discuss driving with your treating team, as local licensing rules vary significantly. You must follow the specific guidelines provided by your doctor and local authorities regarding when it is safe to drive again. Do not guess; rely on your medical team’s advice.

To help us tailor this support, I have two focused questions for you. First, can you describe what you felt or saw immediately before and after each episode? Second, do you have any family history of seizures or neurological conditions?
